cells.tense: You can tell what's worth passing on and what's only still being done.
cells.ask: Offer someone one thing you've made, with no conditions on how they use it.
cells.core:
The thing you made has settled, and you've stopped fussing over whether it's good enough. You can pick up a way of doing something and tell whether it's still carrying weight or just still happening. That's not a small skill, and it's quieter than it looks.

So what you hand on tends to last. It isn't polished — it's chosen. You're not the one protecting every scrap and you're not the one clearing it all out either. You're the one deciding which pieces still have something in them.

So offer one piece to somebody who'll take it and change it. Not keep it as-is — use it. Watch it come back different and let that count as the thing working.
cells.sheetLine: You know what carries, and you keep only that.
cells.verb: to complete the form and hand it on
cells.place: in what gets carried between people and kept

cells.tense: There's a version of this where it's finally done, and you're already living there.
cells.ask: Leave the piece alone for one evening and let someone else's version stand.
cells.core:
You're pushing the finish line further out and paying for it now. The thing needs completing, so you're doing the correcting ahead of time — drafting the ending before it's been built, checking whose version will hold. Everything on the table gets fixed before anyone's read it.

Bracing that hard takes the same grip the finishing needs. Up the road this far, you can't feel what's actually in the room. The work doesn't get complete any faster for being guarded. It gets smaller.

Already there isn't the same as landed, and you won't know which one you've got until you stop steering it. So leave it for one evening and let somebody else's version stand. You can pick it back up tomorrow.

cells.tense: You've got something that could stand on its own, and the last piece stays in the drawer.
cells.ask: Take one piece of it all the way to finished, alone, and don't show anyone yet.
cells.core:
You have something nearly complete and you're not putting the last piece on. The making goes fine — the inside part, the shaping, the polishing where nobody's watching. It's the step where it leaves your hands and stands somewhere in daylight where the brake sits now.

That's not laziness. A finished thing can be looked at, and you've gotten very good at not being looked at. What you've made is still there. The offering stopped.

So take one piece of it all the way to the end by yourself. No audience, no explanation owed to anyone. Give yourself the finished thing first. You can decide later what else happens to it.

cells.tense: You're already deciding what gets kept and passed down, and you call it just how things are done.
cells.ask: Name one choice you made about what gets passed down, out loud, once.
cells.core:
Look at what you've been keeping. You pick what gets kept, what gets said at the table, what gets repeated and what quietly doesn't — and you file it under the family's way, or just what people do here. That happens all day and no one signs it, including you.

You know the moves. When a story comes up you decide whether it lands softer or sharper, whether this telling includes the hard part. That's not temperament. That's an edit, made in real time, and you're not counting it as work.

Pick one of those calls and say, plainly, that it was yours. To yourself first, then out loud if it holds. The call was already made. Saying so just puts your hand back on the pen.
cells.sheetLine: You've been choosing what carries, and calling it how things go.
